2. The appellant as plaintiff instituted the title suit stating, inter alia, that the plaintiff carries on the business as exporter of hides and skins and he collects lizard skins from various persons of Bangladesh and exports the same to foreign countries and that the plaintiff in the past exported a huge quantity of lizard skins after obtaining permission from the Government although the killing of lizards in Bangladesh has been prohibited under the notification of the government dated 27-5-1978 and that the plaintiff collected 1,17,224 pieces of lizard skins and keeping them in 40 wooden boxes under the label tamarind sent the same from Dhaka to Khulna for storage in the godown of Agrani Transport Agency at Khulna under a chalan dated 17-9-1980 and that the plaintiff made application to the Government to accord necessary permission to export the lizard skins and that while the plaintiff was waiting for permission for exporting the goods in the meantime defendant No. 4, Superintendent of Customs and Excise, at the instance of some interested persons, raided the godown of the Agrani Transport Agency and seized the aforesaid 40 boxes of lizard skins of the plaintiff under Customs Act, 1969 and a seizure list dated 22-7-1981 was also prepared and the goods were removed to the customs godown at Khulna and that the Customs Authorities valued the lizard skins at Taka 50,000.00 (Taka fifty thousand) only, and that the plaintiff coming to know of the seizure served a lawyer's notice dated 27-7 -81 praying for release of the goods but the defendant No.3 refused to release the said skins. Thereafter, the defendant No. 3 issued a show cause notice dated 27-8-1981 calling upon the plaintiff to explain as to why the seized goods should not be confiscated to the State and penal action should not be taken against him under the provisions of section 56 of the Customs Act, 1969 read with section 3(3) of Import and Export (Control) Act, 1950. The plaintiff submitted a reply dated 7-9-81 and a supplementary reply dated 21-10-1981 (Exhibit-6 (?) was also later submitted by the plaintiff stating, inter alia, that the allegations stated in the show cause notice do not constitute a case of smuggling or attempt to smuggling under the provisions of section 156 (7) (8) (9) or (90) of Customs Act read with section 3 of Import and Export (Control) Act, 1950 and the present proceedings are without lawful authority and wholly unauthorised. (Vide page 35, part II of the paper book) 

 9. Mr M Faruque, the learned Deputy Attorney-General, on the other hand, appearing for the government respondent, submits that there is a list notified by the government of protected animals i.e. animals which shall not be hunted, killed or captured including the lizard and, as such, the appellant had no right to have possession of the lizard skins in anyway. He further submits that under the provisions of Import and Export (Control) Ordinance, 1950 there is a restriction on the export of lizard skins. In support of his contention the learned Deputy Attorney-General has placed before us the export policy wherein it has been specifically mentioned that the lizard skins is one of the items that has been barred for any export. 

 14. As stated earlier the plaintiff in this suit has sought for a decree for declaration that the order dated 27-2-1984 passed by the Defendant No.1 is illegal, inoperative and void, etc. This order has been marked as Exhibit 7(b). From the said order (vide page-74, part II of the paper book) it appears that the action has been taken by the defendants under the provisions of the Customs Act, 1969 read with the Imports and Exports (Control) Act 1950 and it has been noted in the said order that section 156 (I) (9) (90) provides for confiscation of certain goods.
